text:
Leo: Quick sync — thinking about identity handoff for Private dataplane (sidecar vs relay). Two approaches I've sketched: (A) control-plane mints short-lived mTLS certs and pushes them to sidecars via the agent; (B) customers supply key material (KMS/HSM) and we do a 1‑time attested handshake to establish per-tenant mTLS. Tradeoffs: scalability, rotation/revoke, audit, and operational complexity. Thoughts?

Sara: +1 for short‑lived certs pushed by the agent. Easier to rotate/revoke across fleet. But what if control-plane is unreachable? risk of mass expiry.

Andrew: We should support both. Default to short‑lived certs from CP for PLG/customers, and opt‑in customer‑managed keys for regulated tenants. That buys us simplicity and compliance.

Kevin: If we push certs over the peered/control link we must bind the bootstrap to the VPC/agent identity. Suggest bootstrap token tied to VPC ID + connection fingerprint so a stolen token can't be replayed.

Sana: Also consider using workload identity (cloud IAM) as primary attestation instead of long lived tokens. CP can verify instance identity first, then mint cert. Minimizes secret handling.

infra-bot: deploy-check: controlplane->agent channel encryption verified (sha256:ab12...).

Mike: Proposed handshake sequence (rough):
1) Sidecar connects to local agent and requests bootstrap with local attestation (metadata: VPC, instance-id, sig).
2) Agent relays to control-plane handshake endpoint: POST /bootstrap?token=<token>
3) Control-plane validates attestation + token -> returns cert bundle {cert.pem, key.pem, ca.pem, ttl=15m} or a reference URL to pull behind private relay.
4) Sidecar installs cert and starts mTLS with relay/endpoints.

Example snippet: 
```
POST /bootstrap?token=eyJ... HTTP/1.1
Host: cp-internal.redwood
Content-Type: application/json
{"vpc":"vpc-1234","instance":"i-0abc","sig":"..."}
```

And response contains ephemeral certs (base64).

Sara: Concern: extra egress/requests on every rotation. Can we piggyback rotation on the existing healthcheck/keepalive path so we don't double the traffic?

Andrew: Piggybacking is fine but be careful with payload size. Alternative: CP returns a small reference and sidecar pulls cert over local peered relay only when rotation is due. That reduces CP load.

Leo: Operational notes: audit log events on accept/rotate/revoke are mandatory for enterprise. Also need a fallback path: if CP unavailable and cert expired, sidecar should fall back to cached key or a cached short grace window (configurable) to avoid outages, with strict telemetry to alert.

Kevin: I'll sketch an API surface: /bootstrap, /rotate, /revoke, /attest. Add query params for mode=push|pull and mode=managed|customer. Will open RFC PR this week.

Sana: For on-prem/airgapped installs we need a CSI/volume plugin or in-memory caching because they might ban file writes. Also document how to use HSM-backed keys.

Mike: Also: NAT/hairpinging considerations — if agent talks to CP via NATed egress, make sure token binding to egress IP isn't the only attestation. Use instance metadata instead.

Leo: Agreed. Next steps: Kevin + Mike to draft RFC with sequence diagrams, cost estimate (rotation qps), and failure-mode matrix. If others have constraints (compliance/SOC), add comments on the PR. :thumbsup:
